reason: King Josiah actively demonstrates accountability for the state of the Hebrew people through multiple concrete actions: he tears his garments upon hearing the Torah words, commands his officials to seek the Lord's will, personally gathers all the people and reads the Book of the Covenant to them, makes a covenant before the Lord to keep His commandments, and orchestrates extensive religious reforms to address idolatry and covenant violations throughout the land. The text explicitly states he 'turned to the Lord with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses.' His accountability is further demonstrated by his personal leadership in removing idolatrous items, destroying high places, and celebrating Passover according to the Law.
